meetings.headline: Select Board rehired retired town accountant Karen Brochu as interim finance director amid a stalled recruitment.
meetings.summary: The Lunenburg Select Board ratified Stephen Wallace as the new planning and economic development director, heard a clean FY24 audit from CBIZ that flagged behind-schedule cash and receivable reconciliations and an unresolved ~$90,000 Fitchburg water-billing issue, and approved bringing retired accountant Karen Brochu back part-time as interim finance director after the posted position drew no viable candidates. The board also approved several license renewals, an interim finance director's contract, and a letter to the Governor urging significantly more state local aid (citing a $351 million statewide UGGA ask) ahead of the FY2027 budget process, and opened discussion on the future redevelopment of 925 Mass Ave, appointment policy revisions, and opioid settlement fund planning.

attendees.role: director of planning and economic development (newly appointed), presenter

public_comment.topic: Asked whether the audit and Wallace introduction were public hearings, pressed for a public hearing on the $90,000 owed related to the Fitchburg water billing issue and on school department financial concerns, and criticized lack of interaction during public comment.
Asked what an 'intermittent heavy equipment operator' position is, and suggested the letter to the Governor should also press the state to fund unfunded state mandates.

votes.motion: Ratify the town manager's appointment of Steven Wallace as director of planning and economic development.
Ratify the town manager's appointment of Brandy Oul as meal site manager.
Ratify the town manager's appointment of Joseph Davis as intermittent heavy equipment operator.
Approve the annual license renewals as printed on the agenda, with contingent votes for the applicants with outstanding items (excepting Smokestack, addressed separately).
Approve an additional annual common victualler license renewal that had been omitted from the agenda.
Approve the employment agreement for Karen Brochu as interim finance director/town accountant.
Approve the letter to Governor Healey on local aid and the FY2027 budget, and send copies to the Governor, legislators, the school committee and the finance committee.
Adjourn.

budget_items.what_was_said: The auditor reported the total general fund balance, with portions set aside for encumbrances and free cash used for the FY25 budget, leaving an unassigned balance that rose from the prior year.
The auditor listed balances in the general, zoning, vehicle and equipment, health insurance, and opioid stabilization funds, noting the general stabilization fund has grown steadily since 2013.
The auditor said real estate and personal property tax collections remained strong.
The auditor described a revenue surplus and underspending across departments, offset by use of free cash to balance the FY24 budget.
The town's OPEB trust contribution and investment income grew the fund, while the net OPEB liability fell, tied partly to a higher blended discount rate.

budget_items.topic: Net pension liability, Worcester Regional Retirement System
budget_items.what_was_said: The auditor reported the town's net pension liability rose slightly while the system's funded ratio improved.
Capital asset additions for general government, mainly road paving and equipment, were reported; none for the sewer enterprise.
Short-term debt outstanding funded the capital plan and a land purchase; required long-term debt payments for governmental and sewer funds were noted.
The town exceeded the federal expenditure threshold requiring a single audit, with the education stabilization fund selected for testing and no findings.
A resident and board members discussed money owed related to the town not raising water rates or billing timely when Fitchburg raised its rates; described as an FY25/26 issue outside the FY24 audit.
The town manager reported the MMA is calling for a statewide increase to UGGA to restore pre-recession local aid levels.

budget_items.topic: Finance director recruitment / recruiting agency fee
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said Robert Half would be engaged to help recruit a finance director and payroll/benefits administrator, with a fee only if a hire results.
The board approved contingent votes for several license applicants with outstanding paperwork, inspections, or landlord issues.

budget_items.topic: Employment agreement, interim finance director Karen Brochu
budget_items.what_was_said: A retired former town accountant/finance director agreed to return on an hourly, part-time basis with no additional benefits, capped by retiree earnings limits.
A board member found the MMA's report basis for its ask, benchmarking UGGA against historical local tax share, yielding a similar but not identical figure to what was cited.
A board member reported a one-time reimbursement grant amount for Lunenburg from a fund tied to a regional hospital closure, based on a base amount plus a call-volume formula.
The planning board report noted a completed lot posted a performance guarantee bond, after which the certificate of occupancy could be issued.

decisions.decision: The town will engage CBIZ again for the FY25 audit once FY25 is closed, targeted for around January 31st, with a contract signed before work begins.
When engaging the auditor for FY25, the town manager will request special attention to issues including the Fitchburg water billing matter.
Board members indicated comfort proceeding with contingent votes on pending license renewals, including Lunenburg Gas, rather than delaying or calling a special meeting.
Board members will review the prior Mass Development presentation video (June 11) on 925 Mass Ave before the next discussion.
If any board member wants Mass Development's representative to give a follow-up presentation, they should tell the town manager before the following week.
The board's focus at the next 925 Mass Ave discussion will be the evaluation criteria on pages 16-17 of the draft RFP.
Board flagged for further consideration in January whether/how to structure a subcommittee to screen or interview appointment applicants, given open meeting law implications.
The appointment policy's key dates section will read simply 'June' rather than 'first and second Tuesday in June.'
A future agenda item will be scheduled to decide how the town will approach expenditure of opioid settlement funds.
Board members will coordinate signing the letter to the Governor via DocuSign or in person on another day, since it was not yet printed and a board member was absent.

The state-aid letter touches how much of the FY2027 school and town budget is covered by the state versus local taxpayers.

meetings.headline: Select Board voted a single FY2026 tax rate, rejecting a split rate and all optional exemptions.
meetings.summary: The Select Board held its annual FY2026 tax classification public hearing, at which the principal assessor recommended and the board voted a single tax rate with no residential exemption, open space discount, or small commercial exemption. Public comment also raised concerns about the poorly-run finance committee warrant hearing and about unaccounted Fitchburg charges going undetected for years, urging tighter accounting oversight ahead of budget season.

public_comment.topic: Criticized the finance committee's public hearing on special town meeting warrant articles as poorly run, with no sponsors present and no select board members in attendance.
Asked the board to have the town's auditors explain why charges owed to Fitchburg went unpicked-up for several years, and urged tighter accounting oversight ahead of budget season.
Argued for a split tax rate, citing the tax deferral program for seniors and the need for revenue to fund services such as the senior center.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to set a single FY2026 tax rate for all property classes, rejecting a split rate and all optional exemptions.
Board members signaled they would follow the assessor's recommendation before the formal vote was taken.
The board first closed the tax classification public hearing by unanimous vote after the assessor walked through valuations and the levy calculation.
During public comment, a resident argued for a split rate instead, pointing to the senior tax deferral program and funding for the senior center.
Separate public comment criticized how the finance committee ran its warrant hearing and raised unresolved Fitchburg charges, urging tighter accounting oversight ahead of budget season.

why_it_matters: A single tax rate means residential and commercial property owners share the same rate rather than shifting more of the levy onto commercial parcels, which shapes what every FY2026 tax bill looks like.
Declining the residential exemption, open space discount, and small commercial exemption means no separate tax break exists this year for owner-occupants, open land, or small qualifying businesses.
The accounting concerns raised about the finance committee hearing and Fitchburg charges point to oversight questions the board may face again as budget season begins.

meetings.headline: Town manager says finance-department transition is causing substantial, monthslong operational and financial disruption
meetings.summary: The Select Board heard a Lunenburg Snow Riders equipment gift, ratified three town-hire appointments, and voted to sign a Massachusetts Teachers Association-linked advocacy letter to the state legislature on FY27 school funding over one member's objection about scope and a resident's objection about partisanship. The board worked through special-town-meeting warrant articles (voting recommendations on two planning board articles), heard the town manager describe a difficult and costly finance-department staffing transition and a corrected new-growth figure, and set up scheduling for a pre-town-meeting session and a tri-board meeting with the schools before entering executive session on a non-union personnel matter.

About $140,000 remains in the health insurance stabilization fund, which the town manager would propose using if the retiree health insurance increase cannot otherwise be absorbed.

The town manager plans to bring the salary reserve transfer funding the first year of the new police contract to town meeting as a matter of tradition, with other salary reserve transfers handled directly at town meeting.

what_happened.line: Select Board voted 3-2 to pull the APDC/Historical Commission merger article from the special town meeting warrant.
The vote followed extended public opposition and a town counsel review of legal questions the merger raised.
The board voted 4-1 to recommend the special education reserve fund article, after a member flagged a possible hidden future budget impact.
The noise ordinance article was deferred and will not appear on this warrant, pending further work.
The board voted to include and recommend the 41A senior tax deferral article, raising the decades-old income threshold for that exemption.

why_it_matters: Pulling the merger article means the Architectural Preservation District Commission keeps separate authority over historic-district reviews, at least until a future town meeting takes it up again.
The 41A article, if approved by voters at the November 18 special town meeting, would let more senior homeowners qualify to defer their property tax bills.
The special education reserve fund article changes how the town could set aside money for special-ed costs; it carries no budget impact yet, but a member noted it could down the road.

what_happened.line: The board voted to include a new special-education reserve fund on the Special Town Meeting warrant, capped at 2% of net school spending, with recommendation of approval; how it gets funded is left to a future town meeting.
It voted to include and recommend transferring the Kids Kingdom playground from the School Committee to the Select Board.

It included a bylaw change affecting the Architectural Preservation District on the warrant but held off recommending it after a resident said the change amounts to a zoning shift that has not gone through the Planning Board or a public hearing.
The board reviewed but did not vote on a broad rewrite of the town's personnel bylaw that would dissolve the Personnel Committee and change vacation, sick leave and grievance rules.
The town manager said free cash may not be certified before the warrant prints but is expected by mid-November, which would determine whether some capital items rely on older appropriations instead.

why_it_matters: The special-education reserve fund would let the town cover unanticipated out-of-district placement costs without a town meeting vote, though a board member raised whether it could mask underfunding of the special-education line rather than fix it.

The Architectural Preservation District article affects any resident in that district doing exterior repairs, and a resident's objection that it bypassed the normal zoning-change process could shape whether it comes back for a public hearing before Town Meeting votes on it.

The personnel bylaw rewrite would change how town employees accrue leave and file grievances and who has authority over those decisions, which affects the workforce providing town services even though it is not a resident-facing vote.

meetings.headline: Select Board terminated Flat Hill Road contractor for cause; school's ~$582K FY25 surplus remains unverified
meetings.summary: The Select Board went into executive session over a non-union personnel matter, then ratified three town manager appointments, and heard that the town has terminated its contractor on the Flat Hill Road culvert project for cause. Most of the substantive discussion concerned an approximately $582,000 FY25 school budget surplus reported by the superintendent, which the town manager cautioned could shrink due to outstanding encumbrances and cannot be used until certified as free cash and appropriated at a future town meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: A board member urged residents to watch the school committee meeting that revealed a budget surplus. He called it a source of important ongoing discussion in town.
The town manager said the superintendent sent a memo on September 3rd about a budget surplus, formally shared with the community September 4th.
The town manager explained an encumbrance currently shown on the books that could reduce the reported surplus if the outstanding bills are real.
The town manager said the actual outstanding amount could fall anywhere in that range, which would shrink the surplus accordingly.

budget_items.topic: Free cash process for FY25 surplus
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager explained the surplus must return to the town and become free cash, which can only be appropriated at town meeting, earliest November 18th 2025.
The town manager said the district needs to check whether the same assumptions behind the FY25 numbers were carried into the FY26 budget.
The town manager said she asked directly whether override-funded positions were restored and Chromebooks purchased in FY25, and was told yes to both.

budget_items.topic: Chapter 90 funds for Flat Hill Road project
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said additional chapter 90 funds this year help cover the project, which otherwise might have required more town meeting funding.
The town manager said the original contractor was the lowest bidder by that margin, and a rebid is likely to come in substantially higher.
A board member reported the Capital Planning Committee urged prompt action on budget requests due by October 1st.
A board member reported the assessors' figures for residential, commercial, industrial and chapter land growth and the expected tax value derived from it.
A board member reminded that the warrant for special town meeting is open and closes October 2nd.

decisions.decision: The board agreed to ratify the three town manager appointments in a single motion, with a legal-review caveat noted for Melissa Richard.

what_happened.line: The town terminated its Flat Hill Road culvert contractor for cause; a rebid is expected to cost more than the original contract.
The town manager said a school budget surplus reported by the superintendent could shrink because of encumbrances still on the books.
The surplus cannot be spent until certified as free cash and appropriated at town meeting, no earlier than November 18, 2025.
The Select Board ratified three town manager appointments, including an executive assistant hire pending legal review.
A resident asked that any settlement with the terminated contractor make Flat Hill Road residents whole and exceed the contract value.

why_it_matters: A rebid on the Flat Hill Road culvert project running higher than the terminated contract could add to what the town needs to fund, even with added Chapter 90 aid.
The school surplus is not settled money for residents: it depends on encumbrances still being reconciled and, if confirmed, follows the free cash process before any of it can be spent.
Whether FY25 assumptions behind override-funded positions and Chromebook purchases carried into the FY26 budget is still being checked, which touches what residents already voted to fund.

meetings.headline: Select Board ratified a new multi-year police union contract and raised trash bag fees
meetings.summary: The Select Board recognized its first class of town merit awardees, ratified a new multi-year police union contract, and approved a trash bag fee increase effective in the fall. Members also discussed multiple staff resignations and retirements, reviewed early feedback on the town's draft master plan, and adopted new sick leave bank and gift policies. A resident used public comment to question financial oversight following the finance director's resignation and to ask for a forensic audit.

budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director said trash removal costs have exceeded pay-as-you-throw bag income in FY24 and FY25 and presented 2%, 5%, and 10% increase options, recommending the rounded 5% option effective October 1, 2025.

budget_items.topic: DPW hauling contract with GW Shaw
budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director noted the three-year hauling contract ends in FY27, with an option to extend or rebid, and said costs beyond that point are unknown.

budget_items.topic: Cost of bags to the town
budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director said the town's cost per case of small bags has risen over the years, a small piece of the overall trash program cost compared to hauling.

budget_items.topic: Music Boosters fundraiser and school music supply budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The Music Boosters president reported funds raised at a 'fill the boot' event and asked to send some to Turkey Hill and restore the middle/high school music program's supply budget that had been cut during the budget process.
With the finance director/town accountant resigning, the town manager said she is talking with a vendor about interim financial management support during the transition.

budget_items.topic: MART Council on Aging services agreement, FY2026-2028
budget_items.what_was_said: The board held off on a three-year agreement with the Montachusett Regional Transit Authority for Council on Aging services because a clear comparison of contract changes was not yet available.

The town manager described a ratified three-year contract with annual wage increases, revised education incentive percentages, new stipends, an expanded sick-leave family definition, and a switch to accrual-based vacations; the town will run with three sergeants instead of four to help fund it.

budget_items.topic: Chapter 70 / FY26 omnibus budget amendment (warrant article)
budget_items.what_was_said: A standing warrant article would allow raising, appropriating, borrowing or transferring funds to amend the FY26 omnibus budget; the chair is discussing possible Chapter 70-related changes with the superintendent before bringing it to the board.
Board members said health insurance costs are rising quickly and, if the trend continues, could add roughly a million dollars to costs within three years, calling it a major part of the budget.

budget_items.topic: Water district rate increase and tri-board agenda
budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked that the water district's potential rate increase, which could coincide with a tax increase, be added to the upcoming tri-board meeting agenda.

decisions.decision: Set the trash bag fee increase effective date as October 1, 2025.
Fund part of the new police contract by continuing to run the department with three sergeants instead of the budgeted four.
Chair will discuss potential Chapter 70/FY26 budget amendment ideas with the superintendent privately before raising it publicly.
Town manager will keep a running shared list of potential special town meeting warrant articles as they come in.
Board members will submit individual feedback on the master plan recommendations spreadsheet to the chair (or town manager) to compile.
Adopt the sick leave bank policy now but delay setting an effective date or opening enrollment until the sick leave bank committee is formed.

meetings.headline: Select Board set the fall Special Town Meeting for Nov. 18, 2025, with the warrant opening Aug. 20 and closing Oct. 2.
meetings.summary: The Lunenburg Select Board ratified a new police lieutenant and several other appointments, heard a lengthy update from the assessor's office on reforms since the 2023 lakefront tax crisis, and set the fall Special Town Meeting for November 18, 2025 with its warrant timeline. The board also worked through a list of possible warrant articles, declined to pursue a BYOB alcohol policy change for now, authorized a stormwater grant application, sent a legislative support letter for the Nashoba Associated Boards of Health pension issue, and chose not to vote on accepting an unfinished prior tax investigation report.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager thanked the legislative delegation for securing regional funding for fire and EMS services after the Nashoba Valley Medical Center closure, but said the town would not rely on it for ongoing operations since distribution details are unknown.
The town manager reported Lunenburg Public Schools is receiving a state cyber grant to upgrade three end-of-support network switches.
The town manager reported the final FY26 Chapter 90 apportionment came in well above what was assumed at town meeting, leaving additional funds available for road work.
The town manager relayed rough cost estimates for continuing with the current design firm on Town Hall/Ritter plus Brooks House, versus starting over with a new firm.
The town received one bid for the court resurfacing project that came in under the budgeted amount and is finalizing a contract.

budget_items.topic: Town meeting warrant postcard mailing cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member estimated the cost of mailing a full warrant booklet to every registered voter, part of the case for switching to a postcard notice.
A board member noted the state provided additional Chapter 70 funding and suggested coordinating with the school department on a warrant article to appropriate it.

budget_items.topic: Clean Water SRF grant - asset management inventory
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager described a stormwater asset-mapping project mostly funded by a state grant with the remainder from town funds, requiring board authorization to file the application.
The board accepted a monetary gift from the Lunenburg Friendly Seniors to the Council on Aging.
Two accounts payable warrants were presented to the board without discussion.
The board of assessors liaison reported FY26 growth in assessed value and noted personal property assessed values were lower than the prior year.
The principal assessor cited declining abatement counts as evidence of improved assessing practices compared to the volume issued during the fiscal 2023 lakefront valuation crisis.

decisions.decision: Board agreed in principle to move to a postcard-format town meeting warrant notice with hard copies available on request, and directed that drafting begin; a formal vote will follow when finalized.
Board directed that any warrant article moving additional Chapter 70 state funding to the schools be drafted as an additional appropriation article, with communication to the school department first.

Board declined to commit further resources to researching a BYOB policy change at this time, but was open to the town manager informally asking the requesting business about pursuing a wine/malt pouring license instead.

Board decided not to vote to accept the tax investigation report as submitted and to remove it from the agenda, since none of the current members were involved in the original investigation and the board of assessors has its own corrections pending.
Confirmed a quorum is expected for the August 26 tri-board meeting.
Identified that the board will lack a quorum for the week of September 16 due to two members' absences and will work around it.

meetings.headline: Select Board told the building committee to rescope Ritter/Town Hall, dropping ACE, before returning to voters
meetings.summary: The Select Board spent most of the meeting in a joint session with the Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee, giving direction after the narrow town-meeting/ballot defeat of the Ritter/Town Hall renovation: drop the ACE program from the plan, keep PAC in the building, add an Architectural Preservation District Commission representative, and lower the committee's quorum. The board also heard a legal opinion on the limited authority of the Board of Commissioners of Trust Funds, made several routine committee appointments, declared vehicles and equipment surplus, and received a town manager's report covering the Flat Hill Road bridge repair, sewer delinquency figures, and other items. No new town-meeting date or redesign budget was set.

decisions.decision: The town manager will work with the treasurer/collector and town counsel to try to locate missing trust-fund documentation before any distribution decisions are made.
The facilities director's committee membership will not be decided tonight; the town manager will discuss it with him first given after-hours meeting demands.
The board agreed to keep the committee's charge modification general rather than naming ACE or PAC space changes specifically.
No formal surplus-threshold policy was adopted, but the board indicated interest in letting the town manager surplus low-value items without a board vote in the future.
The board will not take a formal vote on 56 Car A tonight; a vote will follow within 14 days if and after a court judgment enters, per town counsel's guidance.

The board voted unanimously to add an Architectural Preservation District Commission seat and lower the committee's quorum to four members.
The board deferred a vote on the 56 Car A property, saying a vote will follow within 14 days of a court judgment.
The town manager reported sewer delinquency figures that did not support a rate cited at an earlier meeting.
The board directed staff to search for missing documentation on several trust funds before any distribution decision.

why_it_matters: Dropping ACE from the Ritter/Town Hall plan changes what residents will be asked to fund and vote on at a future town meeting or ballot.
Whether the small trust funds can be distributed for their stated purposes depends on documentation the town has not yet located.
Corrected sewer delinquency figures affect what revenue the town can plan for from that fund.
watch_next: No new town-meeting date or redesign budget for Ritter/Town Hall has been set.
A vote on the 56 Car A property, expected within 14 days of a pending court judgment.

meetings.headline: Select Board adopted tri-board ground rules to launch the FY27 school/town budget process, plus several appointments.
meetings.summary: The Select Board handled a full agenda of appointments (Adam Bernie to planning board, Cara McCarthy as communications/IT manager, Tiffany Warren to Cultural Council), heard a town manager report covering a state supplemental school funding award, Wallace Park damage, and staffing vacancies, and reviewed ARPA project balances nearing their spending deadline. Much of the meeting was devoted to setting FY2026 town manager and select board goals and adopting ground rules for a new joint "tri-board" process with the school committee and finance committee aimed at producing a select board recommendation on the FY27 budget, including possible cuts, level funding, or a Prop 2½ override, by around February 2026. The board closed by entering executive session for town manager contract negotiations and police union bargaining strategy.

Defended cemetery superintendent Todd Hullman against what he called unfair, ongoing criticism from board and commission members.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager announced a supplemental state budget allocation for the schools, split among two transportation vans, infrastructure upgrades, and educational materials.
The town manager reported vehicle-accident damage to the fence and play structure at Wallace Park, with an insurance claim filed and an estimate given.
The town manager said MAR Connect, previously funded through a 2024 special town meeting appropriation after losing grant funding, was not carried forward into FY2026 and the program ends.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager relayed a temp agency quote for the vacant executive assistant position that the board considered too costly, prompting a plan to advertise it as a possible contract role instead.

budget_items.topic: Municipal building design project ARPA remainder
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said this remainder's use is pending outstanding invoices and a possible decision on redesign work after town meeting rejected the project.

budget_items.topic: Fire department ambulance / power stretcher ARPA remainders
budget_items.what_was_said: Small ARPA remainders were noted on ambulance-related equipment purchases.
An unexplained remainder was flagged on the six-wheel and ten-wheel dump truck ARPA purchase, to be researched.
A large share of the remaining ARPA balance is committed to two plow trucks ordered in November 2023 and now being upfitted.
The town manager said this remainder is real, with everything eligible already applied, and the parks commission chair will discuss possible uses with the vendor.
A remainder was noted on a completed roof replacement project.
The board discussed the mailing of preliminary tax bills, with quarterly due dates confirmed as August 1 and November 1.

A select board member reported the school committee had discussed level funding, possible cuts, and level services to maintain programs, and discussed the Community Preservation Act as a possible funding source.

transfers.description: Possible movement of small unspent ARPA project remainders into other ARPA projects with shortfalls, if federal guidance allows it

decisions.decision: Planning board (reported to select board) voted to instruct its consultant to draft an MBTA Communities bylaw raising Tritown zoning density from 22 to 26 units per acre, targeting a fall public hearing and special town meeting.
Repost the vacant executive assistant to the town manager/select board position, noting a contract arrangement may be available for the right candidate.
Select board will not add a flag-policy goal now, pending further specific guidance from town counsel, rather than treat it as an immediate priority.
Select board set a target of having a tri-board recommendation on the FY27 budget by February 2026, with tri-board meetings running from July 2025 through the end of January 2026.
First tri-board meeting will be held at the Lunenburg Adult Activity Center; subsequent meetings are expected to be at the library.
No public comment period will be held at the tri-board meetings, though the public may attend and comment at each body's own regular meetings.
Sickle bank policy discussion deferred to a future meeting pending feedback.
Scheduled a site walk of the 56 Carter Seller Hold property for Monday, July 14th at 6 p.m., as a posted meeting.

what_happened.line: The Select Board adopted ground rules for a joint select board/school committee/finance committee "tri-board" process on the FY27 budget.
The board set a target of a tri-board budget recommendation by February 2026, covering cuts, level funding, or a Prop 2½ override.
The board approved revised FY2026 town manager goals and FY26 select board goals.
The board appointed Adam Bernie to the planning board, ratified Cara McCarthy as communications/IT manager, and appointed Tiffany Warren to the Cultural Council.
The town manager reviewed ARPA project balances nearing their spending deadline, including an unexplained remainder on a dump truck purchase to be researched.

why_it_matters: The tri-board process is the mechanism that will produce a recommendation to residents on the FY27 school and town budget, including whether a Proposition 2½ override goes to a vote.
Tri-board meetings will not hold their own public comment period, though residents can still raise budget concerns at each board's regular meetings.
Unspent ARPA funds nearing their deadline touch a parks project, fire department equipment, and a municipal building project, and any unresolved remainder risks being lost.

meetings.headline: Select Board drafted FY26 goals built around a new tri-board process to shape the FY27 budget, override left open.
meetings.summary: The Lunenburg Select Board approved a farmers-market alcohol sampling permit for Pony Shack Cider, then spent nearly the entire meeting drafting FY26 select board and town manager goals. The dominant goal, given top priority, is overhauling the FY27 budget process through new joint 'tri-board' meetings with the finance and school committees, explicitly leaving open the possibility of a town/school Proposition 2½ override; the board also worked through goals on employee experience, transparency, municipal properties (TC Pacios, 925 Main Street, tax title parcels, Brooks House/Municipal Building Design Committee), and policy reviews, without finalizing the goals document that night.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said a professional compensation/classification study, wanted by staff for years, would need outside funding, possibly sought at the fall special town meeting.
The prior SAP bylaw change created a small monetary award for a recognition program; the board discussed removing the money and using a plaque or small gift card instead.

Previously appropriated roof-repair money was designated for a different part of the TC Pacios building than now planned to remain in use; the board wants a fall special town meeting article to move those funds.
A member asked the assessed value of the 925 Main Street property being prepared for sale.
The treasurer/collector is preparing a tax title auction; one parcel's value was cited while discussing which properties boards want to retain.

budget_items.topic: Municipal building capital cost vs. free cash
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted a project cost that would consume the town's entire free cash for a good year, illustrating why it can't be done through ordinary capital planning.

budget_items.topic: Municipal Building Design Committee project cost escalation
budget_items.what_was_said: A member recalled the committee's goal was to keep the prior building project under one figure, but it grew substantially before town meeting rejected it.
Board discussed whether state law only requires an annual report to exist, not to be printed, citing a fine for non-compliance, while considering digitizing it.

budget_items.topic: Cost of printing/mailing town meeting warrant books
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager pulled up the cost of printing and mailing the full warrant book to look at postcard/digital alternatives.
A member asked the town manager to find out how much ARPA money remains unspent this calendar year, since unspent funds are lost after the deadline, with some possible new federal flexibility.

decisions.decision: The board agreed to skip a general Q&A on goal-setting methodology and go straight into reviewing FY25 goals.
The board agreed the FY27 budget process/timeline is the select board's top-priority goal for FY26.
The board defined a new 'tri-board' as regularly scheduled joint meetings of the select board, finance committee, and school committee to prepare the FY27 budget.
Financial policy review/adoption (from the DLS community compact grant) was moved out of the budget goal and made objective one under a separate 'review select board policies' goal instead.
The onboarding/orientation objective for the town manager was tabled for further work rather than finalized that night.
Noted (per the town manager's contract) that goals must be finalized in writing by July 15, with self-evaluation due by April 15 and a November check-in.
Added an action item to bring a fall special town meeting article moving previously appropriated TC Pacios roof-repair funds to the portion of the building that will remain in use.
Agreed the 925 Main Street sale objective will be measured by completion of sale preparation and process, not strictly a completed sale within the fiscal year.
Removed TC Pacios and 925 Main Street from the 'municipal properties' goal draft; folded TC Pacios into the Municipal Building Design Committee objective and added the Brooks House there instead.
Moved the warrant-mailing/postcard bylaw idea into the FY27 budget goal's objectives rather than treating it as a separate goal.
Directed the town manager to report back (targeted for the next meeting) on how much ARPA money remains unspent this calendar year.

The board reorganized after the town election, electing a new chair, vice chair and clerk and seating two newly elected members.

A townwide sick leave bank and the disposition of the 56 Cara Sell property both involve town costs and town-owned property that residents may see come back for a vote or public discussion.

meetings.headline: Select Board again declined to call a special election on the FY26 school override town meeting had approved.
meetings.summary: The Select Board heard extensive public pressure to call a special election on the FY26 Prop 2.5 override that passed narrowly at town meeting, but a majority of members reaffirmed their opposition to putting it on the ballot, citing fiscal concerns and lack of a multi-year plan. The board also set the membership and timeline for a budget task force meant to produce a longer-term fiscal plan, discussed a critical tax investigation report on the 2023 assessment error, approved routine license, appointment, and gift items, and entered executive session on opiate litigation.

meetings.headline: Select Board finalized the town meeting warrant, including a roughly $49M budget and a citizen override question.
meetings.summary: The Select Board reviewed and approved the annual town meeting consent calendar, discussed which officials should move which warrant articles (including an override petition, a school free-cash transfer, and Marshall Park), and heard a Green Communities Committee report on heat-pump grant funding and street-light savings. Town manager updates covered FY26 state aid, project timelines, and staffing vacancies, and a resident used public comment to object to holding town meeting on a Saturday.

The town manager reported the House Ways and Means budget recommends Chapter 70 funded higher than last year with unrestricted government aid level-funded, producing a net increase to Lunenburg's planned aid.
The town manager said residents can buy a pre-bagged town-meeting lunch from the school department.
The Green Communities Committee chair described the grant award and how much of it went toward heat pumps versus other projects like cruisers and refrigeration units.

The committee chair broke down the full project quote for the school heat-pump/central-control retrofit, the grant and rebate portions contingent on the central system, and what would remain for the town if the central unit were skipped.
The committee chair said the town has received close to that much in state grant funding to date through the program.
The chair and committee compared the town's prior monthly street-light bill to the current cost after the LED/Unitil conversion.
The board discussed having the school committee chair, rather than a select board member, move the warrant article transferring free cash to the school since he would answer related questions.

decisions.decision: Board directed staff to press the Ritter building roof/gutter contractor to begin work before the April 30 extension deadline rather than granting another extension without progress.

Board agreed in principle to change the Green Communities Committee's associate members to alternates (or otherwise let associates vote to make quorum), pending confirmation from town counsel that it is legal.

Board agreed the town manager should connect key department heads with the Green Communities Committee over the summer, before the capital plan process, so energy-grant options are considered earlier.
Board decided to leave warrant articles 27 (PEG access/cable), 32 and 33 (board of assessors items) on the consent calendar as-is rather than pulling them off in advance.

what_happened.line: The board voted unanimously to recommend Article 29, the town hall/Ritter/Brooks-area building renovation, for approval at town meeting.
The chair told a State House committee the FY26 school budget faces a large gap that has resulted in staff layoffs.
The board withdrew its recommendation on Article 8, a school capital funding swap, and voted unanimously to defer it pending more information.
The board unanimously ratified Jeffrey Tibido as police chief, contingent on completed contract negotiations.
Multiple residents told the board it had not followed town meeting's direction on exploring a sale or long-term lease of the Brooks House.

why_it_matters: The renovation article now goes to town meeting as a board-recommended article, and if approved would be financed as excludable debt that shows up on the tax bill.
The school budget gap and the resulting layoffs bear on what services and staffing the district can sustain, a live issue as town meeting and any future override discussion approach.
The Brooks House complaints raise whether an elected board is following a direction town meeting already voted, a question about process rather than about any person.

Capital planning committee review of the Article 8 school capital swap before it returns to the board

meetings.headline: Select Board voted not to put the schools' override question on the town election ballot, ending it.
meetings.summary: The Select Board declined to recommend the citizens' petition Proposition 2½ override for the schools and voted separately not to place any override question on the annual town election ballot, ending the override effort for this cycle; members cited a lack of a multi-year plan and the school committee's own non-endorsement. The board also worked through nearly all annual town meeting warrant articles (capital plan, special projects, enterprise funds, a Marshall Park debt exclusion, a school-supplement transfer contingent on the override's failure), reviewed the FY26 SAP salary/COLA plan and a DPW director reclassification, heard an HR report on staff turnover, and voted 4-1 to sign a letter opposing federal library-funding cuts.

budget_items.what_was_said: The finance director and fire chief presented uncollectible ambulance billing to be written off the town's books. They plan to move this to a semiannual process instead of quarterly.
The assistant town manager recommended a 3% COLA for SAP employees instead of the previously budgeted 2.5%, citing the added cost as roughly $43,46, about $7,300 more than the 2.5% option.

budget_items.what_was_said: A warrant article would reclassify the DPW director from grade 16 to grade 17 and create a Communications and IT Manager position without adding headcount; members debated whether one grade increase was enough.
The town manager reported local receipts collected through March against the year's target, noting the collection rate was similar to the same point last year.

The town manager submitted earmark requests under a roughly $50,000 target to the state representative, choosing school security camera server upgrades; the cemetery commission separately renewed a request for monument restoration funding.
The town is putting out a bid for road fog seal and crack seal work with an anticipated total cost and mileage stated.

budget_items.topic: Supplemental transfer to schools contingent on override outcome
budget_items.what_was_said: Article 13 would transfer certified free cash to the Lunenburg schools' FY26 operating budget, but only if the override fails.

budget_items.topic: Impact of the school budget gap if the override fails
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the $2 million shortfall was described to him as equating to the loss of more than 20 teaching positions.
A member noted the school department budget had grown by about 13% over roughly the last two years while the district still faced a shortfall.

budget_items.topic: Estimated tax bill impact of override options
budget_items.what_was_said: A member compared the tax impact of a $2 million override to a larger override, saying the smaller one was more likely to pass with voters.

The town manager recommended no action on these articles this year because free cash is instead being directed to the schools, while noting other reserve funds (OPEB, compensated absences) are still being funded.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted not to put any Proposition 2½ override question on the annual town election ballot, ending the effort this cycle.
The board separately voted not to recommend the citizens' petition override for the schools, citing no multi-year plan and the school committee's own non-endorsement.
The board approved a transfer of free cash to the schools' FY26 budget, but only if the override fails at town meeting.
The board worked through most of the annual town meeting warrant, including removing an unfunded track and field complex article and recommending a Marshall Park debt exclusion.
The board voted 4-1 to sign a congressional letter opposing federal cuts to library and museum funding.

why_it_matters: Residents will not see an override question on this year's town election ballot, so any additional school funding now depends on town meeting votes and the free-cash transfer instead.
The contingent free-cash transfer means the size of the schools' FY26 budget still turns on what town meeting decides about the override article.
The Marshall Park debt exclusion and other warrant articles the board recommended will go to a town-wide vote and can affect the tax bill.

meetings.headline: Select Board backed the pavement plan restored via cuts and a majority refused to put any override on the ballot.
meetings.summary: The board reviewed the town manager's balanced FY26 omnibus budget, including how the pavement management plan was restored through cuts elsewhere, and found a percent-change error for the schools. Members then discussed a citizen-petition school override and a possible town override; a majority said they would not support putting either on the ballot. No formal budget or override vote was taken; the warrant article vote was pushed to a later meeting.

meetings.headline: Select Board and School Committee agreed to skip a FY26 override and use free cash; a larger override is planned for next year.
meetings.summary: A joint session with the School Committee centered on whether to put an override on the May ballot. budget_items.topic: Restoring town-side items with an override
budget_items.what_was_said: Town manager said an override this year would also need to restore pavement management and debt service savings used to balance the budget.
Town manager presented free cash and said it is slightly under the recommended percentage of the budget.
Policy sends a share to OPEB and stabilization funds; the pre-meeting plan totaled a stated amount.
Snow and ice deficiency, special education move-in, a grant clean-up and FY26 capital are funded from free cash, leaving starting free cash for next year.
Town manager could forgo stabilization deposits and use some starting free cash to give about half a million to schools.
Town manager gave the balance and said no spending plan for the fund has been seen.
Town manager presented total revenues, mostly property tax, with new growth estimated conservatively.
State aid is based on the Governor's budget (House 1) with assessments and sweeps netted out.
Motor vehicle excise is a large share of local receipts and may need revisiting before town meeting; investment income has been far above projection.
Town manager walked through the new revenue and its split between town, schools and Monty Tech.
General stabilization is above the 5% target; OPEB transfer of 10% of free cash is the policy; OPEB is lightly funded against a large liability.
Special projects article covers decommissioning, assessor directives and road repair; snow and ice deficit projected; CARES grant clearing.
Debt roll-off lowers debt service; part supports the capital plan and the remainder balances the operating budget, which is not best practice.
Health insurance rises sharply but the line was budgeted closer to actual; Medicare, salary reserve and unemployment (if layoffs occur) noted.
The budget holds funds for grant help that went unused; town manager suggested a grant and contract manager; board split on grant writer versus manager.

what_happened.line: The Select Board spent most of the meeting workshopping a draft employee climate survey policy and did not adopt it.
By consensus the board moved the survey timeline so results arrive about November 1 and set the survey to run every two years instead of annually.
The board kept the final choice of survey vendor and questions for itself and again asked for the full engagement survey results and the vendor's draft questions.

why_it_matters: A survey every two years run by an outside vendor would add a recurring consultant cost to the town-side budget, and the board wanted the timing set sooner than a split across two fiscal years would allow.
The retirement assessment taking up about half of expected new town-side revenue leaves less room for other town services under the levy limit.
The 55 Carver Avenue property and the Community Preservation Act steps both remain open, and a CPA surcharge would be a vote residents are asked to take.
watch_next: The survey policy returning to the board for adoption, with the full engagement survey results and the vendor's draft questions the board requested.
A board decision on whether to retain 55 Carver Avenue through the tax title process.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-1 to appoint Jennifer Warren Diamond as town manager, pending successful contract negotiation.
The board opened the annual town meeting warrant on January 15 and set it to close March 17; the vote was unanimous.
The board supported an internal January 31 deadline for warrant articles not brought by citizen petition.
The board agreed to hold a possible January 28 meeting in case contract negotiations need it.
A consultant said that if talks with the chosen candidate stall, the board can come back and decide again.

why_it_matters: The appointment sets who will lead the town's day-to-day operations and prepare the budget that residents vote on at town meeting, but it is not final until a contract is negotiated.
The warrant timeline fixes when articles, including any money requests, must be submitted before they reach the town meeting ballot and warrant booklet.
watch_next: A possible Select Board meeting on January 28 for contract negotiations.
The warrant closing on March 17, with an internal deadline of January 31 for non-citizen-petition articles.

what_happened.line: The Select Board advised the building committee to fold PACK studio space into phases one and two of the municipal building project and to consider 30 School Street.
The board voted unanimously to accept the comparable communities list as modified, with Gardner added back.
After a joint executive session on litigation, the board jointly appointed a library trustee by roll call for the remainder of a term ending May 2025.
The board agreed that town manager finalist interviews will be held at the library, with redacted resumes and cover letters attached to the agenda.
The board took no action on the 56 Car property while counsel explores whether deed restrictions can be applied.

why_it_matters: Where PACK is housed affects the cost of the new municipal building, and the minutes record the chair saying total cost could rise beyond the original budget, so residents may later be asked to fund more than first presented.
PACK runs on cable franchise fees that are declining and cover operations but not capital, so a standalone building or a major equipment failure would have to be paid for from other sources.
The comparable communities list is the yardstick for salary and budget comparisons, including the town manager search, so which towns are on it shapes later pay and spending arguments.
watch_next: The chair's advice to the architects and the Municipal Building Design Committee on PACK in phases one and two, and any revised cost estimate.
A future agenda item on public records requests, including estimated staff cost, and the Jan 15 meeting, requested for 6 p.m.
